source_lines_after.excerpt: 7.1 The zero operator and zero Hilbert space are covered by step 1.1; on $H=\mathbb C$ with $T=tI$, the determinant is $1+zt$, so for $t\ne0$ its zero is simple and $m_{\mathrm{alg}}(t;T)=1$, while $t=0$ has no zero and every $I+zT$ is invertible. An empty nonzero spectrum yields no noninvertible $I+zT$ by step 5.1. There is no interval parameter or one-sided endpoint. The exact assumption is AC [A1]; it is used through the Riesz–Schauder, Riesz-projection, and algebraic-multiplicity suppliers, and AC supplies the AC$_\omega$ required by the local determinant and trace-class suppliers through [A15]. The finite Jordan-string argument makes no additional choice. Both iff directions were proved in step 6.1; the multiplicity assertion is a factorization claim, not an iff. [A1, A4, A15, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎
